Transformer通过多头注意力机制对线性投影后的键、值和查询进行注意力计算，在大模型设定下于WMT 2014英法翻译任务中取得了41.0的BLEU得分。

results.title: AR-RAG: Autoregressive Retrieval Augmentation for Image Generation
results.abstract: We introduce Autoregressive Retrieval Augmentation (AR-RAG), a novel paradigm that enhances image generation by autoregressively incorporating knearest neighbor retrievals at the patch level. Unlike prior methods that perform a single, static retrieval before generation and condition the entire generation on fixed reference images, AR-RAG performs context-aware retrievals at each generation step, using prior-generated patches as queries to retrieve and incorporate the most relevant patch-level visual references, enabling the model to respond to evolving generation needs while avoiding limitations (e.g., over-copying, stylistic bias, etc.) prevalent in existing methods. To realize AR-RAG, we propose two parallel frameworks: (1) Distribution-Augmentation in Decoding (DAiD), a training-free plug-and-use decoding strategy that directly merges the distribution of model-predicted patches with the distribution of retrieved patches, and (2) Feature-Augmentation in Decoding (FAiD), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that progressively smooths the features of retrieved patches via multi-scale convolution operations and leverages them to augment the image generation process. We validate the effectiveness of AR-RAG on widely adopted benchmarks, including Midjourney-30K, GenEval and DPG-Bench, demonstrating significant performance gains over state-of-the-art image generation models.

results.title: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution
results.abstract: Generation with source attribution is important for enhancing the verifiability of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. However, existing approaches in RAG primarily link generated content to document-level references, making it challenging for users to locate evidence among multiple content-rich retrieved documents. To address this challenge, we propose Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution (VISA), a novel approach that combines answer generation with visual source attribution. Leveraging large vision-language models (VLMs), VISA identifies the evidence and highlights the exact regions that support the generated answers with bounding boxes in the retrieved document screenshots. To evaluate its effectiveness, we curated two datasets: Wiki-VISA, based on crawled Wikipedia webpage screenshots, and Paper-VISA, derived from PubLayNet and tailored to the medical domain. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of VISA for visual source attribution on documents' original look, as well as highlighting the challenges for improvement. Code, data, and model checkpoints will be released.

results.title: Passage Attribution for Evidence-Grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation under Noisy Retrieval
results.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation has emerged as a dominant paradigm for mitigating hallucinations in large language models by grounding generated responses in external knowledge sources. However, the efficacy of these systems is fundamentally bottlenecked by the quality of the retrieved documents. In real-world applications, retrieval components frequently return noisy, irrelevant, or contradictory passages, which can severely degrade the factual accuracy and coherence of the generated output. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into passage attribution mechanisms designed to fortify evidence-grounded generation under conditions of high retrieval noise. We introduce a novel architectural framework that dynamically evaluates and assigns attribution scores to retrieved passages before generation, enabling the language model to selectively attend to highly relevant evidence while discarding spurious noise. Through extensive theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation across multiple domain-specific datasets, we demonstrate that explicit passage attribution not only improves response factuality but also enhances the interpretability of the generation process. Our findings indicate that integrating dynamic thresholding and robust training objectives significantly increases the resilience of generative models against adversarial or noisy retrieval outcomes. The proposed methodology establishes a new benchmark for developing trustworthy, verifiable, and noise-resilient natural language processing systems.

results.title: Adaptive Retrieval and Evidence Calibration for Reliable Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can expose a response to incorrect evidence when a retrieved source is plausible but mismatched. This paper presents ACRE, a compact pipeline that couples query-dependent reranking depth, source-evidence confidence estimation, and a selective output decision. A BM25 candidate list is augmented with lexical similarity signals; logistic confidence models select one, three, or five candidates and determine whether a verbatim, source-attributed answer should be issued. We evaluate on 300 authentic news reports and 50 out-of-index reports from the Lee text corpora, using 1,400 reproducibly derived source-identification queries. On the 280-query held-out split, adaptive retrieval matches the BM25 top-1 source accuracy of 77.86% while requiring only 1.73 candidates per query in the assigned reranking depth, versus five for the fixed-depth alternative. With the development-selected abstention threshold, the system responds to 80.36% of test queries at 91.11% accepted-source accuracy; its expected calibration error is 0.039. The results demonstrate an economical approach to coupling retrieval efficiency with calibrated source attribution in an explicitly extractive RAG setting.

results.title: Identity-Decoupled Anonymization for Visual Evidence in Multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: Multi-modal retrieval-augmented generation (MRAG) systems retrieve visual evidence from large image corpora to ground the responses of large multi-modal models, yet the retrieved images frequently contain human faces whose identities constitute sensitive personal information. Existing anonymization techniques that destroy the non-identity visual cues that downstream reasoning depends on or fail to provide principled privacy guarantees. We propose Identity-Decoupled MRAG, a framework that interposes a generative anonymization module between retrieval and generation. Our approach consists of three components: (i)a disentangled variational encoder that factorizes each face into an identity code and a spatially-structured attribute code, regularized by a mutual-information penalty and a gradient-based independence term; (ii)a manifold-aware rejection sampler that replaces the identity code with a synthetic one guaranteed to be both distinct from the original and realistic; and (iii)a conditional latent diffusion generator that synthesizes the anonymized face from the replacement identity and the preserved attributes, distilled into a latent consistency model for low-latency deployment. Privacy is enforced through a multi-oracle ensemble of face recognition models with a hinge-based loss that halts optimization once identity similarity drops below the impostor-regime threshold.

results.title: How Do LLMs Cite? A Mechanistic Interpretation of Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) aims to enhance the trustworthiness of Large Language Models (LLMs) by grounding their outputs in external documents, often using inline citations for verifiability. However, the faithfulness of these citations -- whether the model genuinely uses a source to generate an answer -- remains a critical, unverified assumption. This paper offers the first mechanistic account of how a large language model decides whether to attach an inline citation while answering a factoid question. Using the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model in a controlled experimental environment based on the PopQA dataset, we employ an activation patching approach. We map the underlying mechanism responsible for citation, discovering that it is not a single, localized component but a distributed, multi-stage "attributional ensemble" of attention heads and MLP layers. We show that amplifying or attenuating only those critical heads and MLPs repairs over 90% of missed citations and eliminates 69% of spurious ones on PopQA without harming answer accuracy. Although gains on the multi-document HotpotQA benchmark are modest, the same component set still moves citation rates in the intended direction, indicating that the underlying mechanism is not dataset-specific. The results reveal a potential disconnect between the model's apparent reasoning and its internal computational pathway, suggesting that inline citations can create a false sense of security.

results.title: Intelligent Interaction Strategies for Context-Aware Cognitive Augmentation
results.abstract: Human cognition is constrained by processing limitations, leading to cognitive overload and inefficiencies in knowledge synthesis and decision-making. Large Language Models (LLMs) present an opportunity for cognitive augmentation, but their current reactive nature limits their real-world applicability. This position paper explores the potential of context-aware cognitive augmentation, where LLMs dynamically adapt to users' cognitive states and task environments to provide appropriate support. Through a think-aloud study in an exhibition setting, we examine how individuals interact with multi-modal information and identify key cognitive challenges in structuring, retrieving, and applying knowledge. Our findings highlight the need for AI-driven cognitive support systems that integrate real-time contextual awareness, personalized reasoning assistance, and socially adaptive interactions. We propose a framework for AI augmentation that seamlessly transitions between real-time cognitive support and post-experience knowledge organization, contributing to the design of more effective human-centered AI systems.

results.title: Automated Literature Review Using NLP Techniques and LLM-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: This research presents and compares multiple approaches to automate the generation of literature reviews using several Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a Large Language Model (LLM). The ever-increasing number of research articles provides a huge challenge for manual literature review. It has resulted in an increased demand for automation. Developing a system capable of automatically generating the literature reviews from only the PDF files as input is the primary objective of this research work. The effectiveness of several Natural Language Processing (NLP) strategies, such as the frequency-based method (spaCy), the transformer model (Simple T5), and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with Large Language Model (GPT-3.5-turbo), is evaluated to meet the primary objective. The SciTLDR dataset is chosen for this research experiment and three distinct techniques are utilized to implement three different systems for auto-generating the literature reviews. The ROUGE scores are used for the evaluation of all three systems. Based on the evaluation, the Large Language Model GPT-3.5-turbo achieved the highest ROUGE-1 score, 0.364. The transformer model comes in second place and spaCy is at the last position. Finally, a graphical user interface is created for the best system based on the large language model.

results.title: FAIR-RAG: Faithful Adaptive Iterative Refinement for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates hallucination and knowledge staleness in Large Language Models (LLMs), existing frameworks often falter on complex, multi-hop queries that require synthesizing information from disparate sources. Current advanced RAG methods, employing iterative or adaptive strategies, lack a robust mechanism to systematically identify and fill evidence gaps, often propagating noise or failing to gather a comprehensive context. We introduce FAIR-RAG, a novel agentic framework that transforms the standard RAG pipeline into a dynamic, evidence-driven reasoning process. At its core is an Iterative Refinement Cycle governed by a module we term Structured Evidence Assessment (SEA). The SEA acts as an analytical gating mechanism: it deconstructs the initial query into a checklist of required findings and audits the aggregated evidence to identify confirmed facts and, critically, explicit informational gaps. These gaps provide a precise signal to an Adaptive Query Refinement agent, which generates new, targeted sub-queries to retrieve missing information. This cycle repeats until the evidence is verified as sufficient, ensuring a comprehensive context for a final, strictly faithful generation. We conducted experiments on challenging multi-hop QA benchmarks, including HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MusiQue. In a unified experimental setup, FAIR-RAG significantly outperforms strong baselines. On HotpotQA, it achieves an F1-score of 0.453 -- an absolute improvement of 8.3 points over the strongest iterative baseline -- establishing a new state-of-the-art for this class of methods on these benchmarks. Our work demonstrates that a structured, evidence-driven refinement process with explicit gap analysis is crucial for unlocking reliable and accurate reasoning in advanced RAG systems for complex, knowledge-intensive tasks.

results.title: EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation
results.abstract: Recently the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has been successfully applied in code generation. However, existing pipelines for retrieval-augmented code generation (RACG) employ static knowledge bases with a single source, limiting the adaptation capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to domains they have insufficient knowledge of. In this work, we develop a novel pipeline, EVOR, that employs the synchronous evolution of both queries and diverse knowledge bases. On two realistic settings where the external knowledge is required to solve code generation tasks, we compile four new datasets associated with frequently updated libraries and long-tail programming languages, named EVOR-BENCH. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EVOR achieves two to four times of execution accuracy compared to other methods such as Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2024), DocPrompting (Zhou et al., 2023), etc. We demonstrate that EVOR is flexible and can be easily combined with them to achieve further improvement. Further analysis reveals that EVOR benefits from the synchronous evolution of queries and documents and the diverse information sources in the knowledge base. We hope that our studies will inspire more insights into the design of advanced RACG pipelines in future research. Our model, code, and data are available at https://arks-codegen.github.io.

results.title: Riddle Me This! Stealthy Membership Inference for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate grounded responses by leveraging external knowledge databases without altering model parameters. Although the absence of weight tuning prevents leakage via model parameters, it introduces the risk of inference adversaries exploiting retrieved documents in the model's context. Existing methods for membership inference and data extraction often rely on jailbreaking or carefully crafted unnatural queries, which can be easily detected or thwarted with query rewriting techniques common in RAG systems. In this work, we present Interrogation Attack (IA), a membership inference technique targeting documents in the RAG datastore. By crafting natural-text queries that are answerable only with the target document's presence, our approach demonstrates successful inference with just 30 queries while remaining stealthy; straightforward detectors identify adversarial prompts from existing methods up to ~76x more frequently than those generated by our attack. We observe a 2x improvement in TPR@1%FPR over prior inference attacks across diverse RAG configurations, all while costing less than $0.02 per document inference.

results.title: Choosing Evidence Before Answering: Decision-Based Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: We examine a variable-count evidence-selection policy for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Embedding retrieval identifies candidates; the OpenAI Decisions API scores their support for a question; deterministic rules admit passages under a relevance threshold and a token budget. Two pilot experiments use 150 authentic passages from two European Central Bank reports and four questions. The first comprises 120 trials comparing scoring batch sizes of 5, 25 and 150. The second comprises 80 paired comparisons of an embedding-based baseline and Decisions selection at requested counts of 5 and 30. Against frozen AI-authored reference annotations, at N=5 mean selected-evidence precision rises from 55.00% to 72.85% and required-fact coverage from 60.42% to 93.75%, while median passage count rises from 5 to 13.5. At N=30, precision rises from 35.75% to 63.23% and coverage from 93.75% to 100%, while median count falls from 30 to 25. Decisions increases estimated retrieval latency, and every trial retains some wrong-edition evidence. These are descriptive comparisons of complete selection policies: candidate admission and output counts differ, only four independent questions are studied, reference judgments are not human-adjudicated, and generated answers are not evaluated. The findings motivate controlled, human-annotated studies of evidence selection and multi-question research under shared budgets. <br><br>AI disclosure: OpenAI Codex was used for research assistance, benchmark preparation, coding, drafting and editorial revision. The reference annotations were produced by gpt-6-luna with targeted review by GPT-6.1 Sol; the evaluated Decisions scorer also used gpt-6-luna. AI-generated reference judgments were not human-adjudicated. The author is responsible for the manuscript and its claims.

results.title: Counterfactual Evidence Repair for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Selective Reliability under Source Shift
results.abstract: RAG failures vary. A response may lack decisive support, be distracted by irrelevant context, rely on stale evidence, or face conflicting sources, and may require different interventions. We examine RAG reliability as a coupled problem of evidence repair and selective answering. A 240-case, four-class benchmark evaluates each case in failure, substantive-repair, and sham states with two open-weight readers. On the correct-and-supported endpoint, substantive repair improves performance by 44.2 percentage points for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (95% paired bootstrap CI 37.5-50.4) and 31.7 points for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 (25.0-37.9), with effects varying by failure class. A six-action in-distribution policy and a counterfactual repair-value (CRV) estimator provide predictive signal under a frozen sham-proxy target; they do not constitute a full action oracle or a cost-optimal policy. Post-repair signals also improve risk estimation, but the pre-specified finite-sample unsupported-answer certificate is underpowered and therefore not established. Source shift exposes a sharper limitation: on CONFACT, the original flat typed policy abstains on 99.3% of cases, so the original robustness hypothesis is not supported. We retain that negative result and evaluate a separately frozen applicability-aware redesign on held-out AVeriTeC. It reaches 46.84% coverage and, among accepted cases, 95.50% selective accuracy (4.50% selective error); overall accuracy when abstentions are counted as non-correct is 44.73%. Most accepted cases are handled by fallback rather than direct typed-policy transfer. Taken together, the results support typed repair inside the learned applicability region while showing that source shift requires an explicit mechanism for recognizing when that policy should not be used.

results.title: Factually: Exploring Wearable Fact-Checking for Augmented Truth Discernment
results.abstract: Wearable devices are transforming human capabilities by seamlessly augmenting cognitive functions. In this position paper, we propose a voice-based, interactive learning companion designed to amplify and extend cognitive abilities through informal learning. Our vision is threefold: (1) to enable users to discover new knowledge on-the-go through contextual interactive quizzes, fostering critical thinking and mindfulness, (2) to proactively detect misinformation, empowering users to critically assess information in real time, and (3) to provide spoken language correction and prompting hints for second language learning and effective communication. As an initial step toward this vision, we present Factually - a proactive, wearable fact-checking system integrated into devices like smartwatches or rings. Factually discreetly alerts users to potential falsehoods via vibrotactile feedback, helping them assess information critically. We demonstrate its utility through three illustrative scenarios, highlighting its potential to extend cognitive abilities for real-time misinformation detection. Early qualitative feedback suggests that Factually can enhance users' fact-checking capabilities, offering both practical and experiential benefits.

results.title: Evaluating Evidence Sensitivity and Robustness of Hallucination Detectors in Retrieval- Augmented Generation
results.abstract:
Abstract
                Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the accessibility of external knowledge for large language models, but generated responses can remain unsupported, contradictory, or otherwise hallucinatory. Conventional hallucination-detector evaluation largely emphasizes aggregate benchmark performance, which may not reveal whether detector decisions remain reliable when the evidence distribution changes. This study presents a controlled evaluation of hallucination detectors from an evidence-sensitivity and robustness perspective. Three detector configurations - TF-IDF with Logistic Regression, TF-IDF with Linear Support Vector Machine, and DeBERTa-v3-base were evaluated using RAGTruth, HaluBench, and TRIVIA+. In-domain evaluation on RAGTruth showed that DeBERTa achieved an AUROC of 0.8483 and Macro-F1 of 0.7616. However, performance declined substantially under distribution shift, with AUROC decreasing to 0.5348 on HaluBench and 0.5910 on TRIVIA+. Controlled evidence interventions showed substantial detector responsiveness, with mean Evidence Sensitivity Index values of 0.2641 for evidence removal and 0.3268 for cross-example evidence substitution. A context-complexity stress test further showed progressive degradation as irrelevant evidence increased from 0% to 100% within a fixed 512-token observation window, with AUROC decreasing from 0.8306 to 0.7325 and Expected Calibration Error increasing from 0.1375 to 0.4072. Input ablation demonstrated that both generated answers and retrieved evidence contribute to detection performance. These findings show that benchmark accuracy alone is insufficient to characterize hallucination-detector reliability and motivate evaluation frameworks that jointly assess generalization, evidence sensitivity, contextual robustness, and calibration.

results.title: Operationalizing Evidence Admissibility in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: The DCA-TRAG Architecture
results.abstract: <p>Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems increasingly support enterprise decision-making over repositories that evolve through revisions, supersession, expiration, and policy updates. Under these conditions, semantic relevance alone cannot guarantee that retrieved evidence is valid for the decision context, allowing inadmissible documents to influence downstream reasoning. This paper introduces Document Churn-Aware Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (DCA-TRAG), a deterministic retrieval architecture that establishes evidence eligibility before semantic ranking through explicit admissibility enforcement. We also introduce the Regulatory Churn Evaluation Framework (RCEF) and admissibility-centric metrics for evaluating retrieval correctness under document churn. DCA-TRAG was evaluated using controlled repository simulations, five retrieval baselines, a production-class LLM temporal-reasoning baseline, statistical validation, and a preliminary real-world assessment using Consumer Financial Protection Bureau guidance. Across all evaluations, deterministic admissibility enforcement consistently improved retrieval correctness and remained robust under evolving repository conditions. These findings demonstrate that retrieval correctness depends not only on semantic relevance but also on deterministic evidence eligibility, providing an architectural foundation for trustworthy enterprise RAG.</p>

results.title: Adaptive Visual Evidence Verification for Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation
results.abstract: Visual retrieval-augmented generation (Visual RAG) answers questions by grounding vision-language models in retrieved page images, thereby preserving layout and graphical evidence that may be lost during OCR-based text conversion. However, retrieved pages may contain irrelevant or misleading cues, while frozen generators can produce inconsistent answers across reasoning paths. To address these issues, we propose Adaptive Visual Evidence Verification (AVEV), a training-free post-retrieval evidence-control framework that integrates ordered-rule evidence pruning, multi-path consensus voting, and conditional re-reading. AVEV conservatively filters distractors while retaining sufficient evidence, aggregates candidate answers to stabilize prediction, and allocates an additional reasoning pass to unresolved Stage-1 outputs. Experiments on five visual question-answering benchmarks show higher reported answer-metric point estimates on four datasets, with the clearest gains on DocVQA. Further analyses of module contributions, repeated inference, cross-backbone transfer, parameter sensitivity, and inference behavior clarify how the components cooperate and support selective evidence processing. Overall, AVEV provides a unified and controllable mechanism for post-retrieval evidence use in frozen Visual RAG systems.

results.title: Explainable Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Evidence-Aligned and Faithful Legal Reasoning
results.abstract:
Abstract
                Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as an effective paradigm for legal question answering, but existing systems often suffer from hallucinated citations and weak evidence grounding. This paper proposes EL-RAG, an explainable retrieval-augmented generation framework designed to ensure evidence-aligned and faithful legal reasoning. The framework formulates evidence grounding as a probabilistic multi-objective optimization problem, integrating a hybrid sparse–dense retriever, a learning-to-rank reranker, a multi-hop reasoning generator, and an Evidence Alignment Layer (EAL). Two evaluation metrics—Citation Alignment Score (CAS) and Faithful Justification Index (FJI) are introduced to assess grounding and interpretability. Experiments on COLIEE 2025, NyayaRAG 2025, CaseLawBench, and LegalBench-RAG show consistent improvements over strong baselines, significantly reducing hallucinations and improving expert-rated interpretability.

source_candidates.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
source_candidates.abstract: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

source_candidates.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
source_candidates.abstract: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

source_candidates.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
source_candidates.abstract: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.

source_candidates.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
source_candidates.abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

source_candidates.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
source_candidates.abstract: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $φ^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.

source_candidates.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
source_candidates.abstract: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

source_candidates.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
source_candidates.abstract: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

source_candidates.title: Limitations of nonreversible lifts for subgeometric diffusions
source_candidates.abstract: We study the effect of lifting on continuous-time Markov processes with potentially subgeometric convergence rates. Using a series of weak Poincaré-type inequalities, we derive a bound on the maximum acceleration that can be obtained through lifting. We present several examples to explore the sharpness of our derived bound, where the resulting bound has the same square-root order as in the spectral gap setting. Our results provide a framework for understanding the potential and limitations of non-reversible lifting beyond geometric convergence.

source_candidates.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
source_candidates.abstract: Slope change detection seeks to identify changes in the trends of time-ordered signals. We study the problem of fitting a multidimensional time series by continuous piecewise-linear functions with a shared continuous breakpoint and unrestricted slopes. We consider both the dense setting, in which every dimension may change slope, and the sparse setting, in which at most $k$ dimensions may change slope. Although the resulting optimization problems are nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear programs and may have irrational optimal solutions even for rational data, we prove that all six variants, corresponding to the $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, and $\ell_\infty$ losses in both settings, are exactly solvable in polynomial time. For least-squares loss, we obtain efficient algorithms requiring $O(JT)$ operations in the dense setting and $O(J^2T\log J)$ operations in the sparse setting, where $T$ is the number of time points and $J$ is the number of dimensions. We implement these least-squares algorithms and evaluate them on simulated data and three real-world time series, namely, surface temperatures (ERA5), hand-tracking data from a mixed-reality headset (HoloAssist), and turbofan engine sensor data (NASA C-MAPSS). The dense algorithm solves instances with up to $J=10^5$ and $T=100$, that is, $10^7$ observations, in less than $0.1$ seconds on a laptop, while the sparse algorithm solves instances with about $10^3$ dimensions and up to $T=240$ in under a second. Compared with a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) formulation solved by Gurobi, our algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster (approximately $8.9 \times 10^3$ to $3.4 \times 10^6$ times) on instances where Gurobi terminates within its default optimality tolerance of $0.01\%$ optimality gap. On larger instances, Gurobi frequently reaches a 10,000-second time limit with substantial optimality gaps.

source_candidates.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
source_candidates.abstract: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption. This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots. Additionally, real-time implementation of this model can be achieved, meeting the demand for computational efficiency in robotic applications. Experimental validations demonstrated that this model is able to reduce the maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm in the frictionless model to 5.85 mm in our friction-included model with a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot.

results.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
results.abstract: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

results.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
results.abstract: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.

results.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
results.abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

results.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
results.abstract: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $φ^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.

results.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
results.abstract: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

results.title: Limitations of nonreversible lifts for subgeometric diffusions
results.abstract: We study the effect of lifting on continuous-time Markov processes with potentially subgeometric convergence rates. Using a series of weak Poincaré-type inequalities, we derive a bound on the maximum acceleration that can be obtained through lifting. We present several examples to explore the sharpness of our derived bound, where the resulting bound has the same square-root order as in the spectral gap setting. Our results provide a framework for understanding the potential and limitations of non-reversible lifting beyond geometric convergence.

results.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
results.abstract: Slope change detection seeks to identify changes in the trends of time-ordered signals. We study the problem of fitting a multidimensional time series by continuous piecewise-linear functions with a shared continuous breakpoint and unrestricted slopes. We consider both the dense setting, in which every dimension may change slope, and the sparse setting, in which at most $k$ dimensions may change slope. Although the resulting optimization problems are nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear programs and may have irrational optimal solutions even for rational data, we prove that all six variants, corresponding to the $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, and $\ell_\infty$ losses in both settings, are exactly solvable in polynomial time. For least-squares loss, we obtain efficient algorithms requiring $O(JT)$ operations in the dense setting and $O(J^2T\log J)$ operations in the sparse setting, where $T$ is the number of time points and $J$ is the number of dimensions. We implement these least-squares algorithms and evaluate them on simulated data and three real-world time series, namely, surface temperatures (ERA5), hand-tracking data from a mixed-reality headset (HoloAssist), and turbofan engine sensor data (NASA C-MAPSS). The dense algorithm solves instances with up to $J=10^5$ and $T=100$, that is, $10^7$ observations, in less than $0.1$ seconds on a laptop, while the sparse algorithm solves instances with about $10^3$ dimensions and up to $T=240$ in under a second. Compared with a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) formulation solved by Gurobi, our algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster (approximately $8.9 \times 10^3$ to $3.4 \times 10^6$ times) on instances where Gurobi terminates within its default optimality tolerance of $0.01\%$ optimality gap. On larger instances, Gurobi frequently reaches a 10,000-second time limit with substantial optimality gaps.

results.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
results.abstract: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

results.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
results.abstract: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption. This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots. Additionally, real-time implementation of this model can be achieved, meeting the demand for computational efficiency in robotic applications. Experimental validations demonstrated that this model is able to reduce the maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm in the frictionless model to 5.85 mm in our friction-included model with a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot.
